description:
DeleteStream removes one stream of the caller's org — its retained messages
and its consumers with it — and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the org
has no stream of that name.

stream.description: Stream is the stream's name, from the path.

name: delete_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream

description:
DeleteConsumer removes one consumer — its cursor, not the stream's messages —
and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the stream or the consumer does not
exist.

name.description: Name is the consumer, from the path.

stream.description: Stream is the stream, from the path.

name: delete_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream_consumers_name

description:
DeleteBucket removes one bucket of the caller's org — every key and every
revision with it — and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the org has no
bucket of that name.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket's name, from the path.

name: delete_v1_pubsub_kv_bucket

description:
Delete removes one key — a delete marker in the key's history, so watchers
see it and Get answers 404 — and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the
bucket does not exist.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

name: delete_v1_pubsub_kv_bucket_key

description:
ListStreams returns the org's streams, sorted by name.

A stream is the durable log: it captures every message published to its
subjects and retains them by its own limits, independent of any consumer.
The listing is org-scoped server-side — one org can never see another's
streams, and the platform's own planes never appear.
name: get_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams

description:
GetStream returns one stream of the caller's org — its configuration and its
live state (messages, bytes, sequence range, consumer count). 404 when the
org has no stream of that name.

stream.description: Stream is the stream's name, from the path.

name: get_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream

description:
ListConsumers returns one stream's consumers, sorted by name. 404 when the
org has no stream of that name.

stream.description: Stream is the stream's name, from the path.

name: get_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream_consumers

description:
GetConsumer returns one consumer of one org stream — its configuration and
its cursor: delivered and acknowledged sequences, pending and redelivered
counts. 404 when the stream or the consumer does not exist.

name.description: Name is the consumer, from the path.

stream.description: Stream is the stream, from the path.

name: get_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream_consumers_name

description:
Get returns one key's current value and revision. 404 when the bucket does
not exist, the key was never written, or its latest revision is a delete.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

name: get_v1_pubsub_kv_bucket_key

description:
History returns one key's retained revisions, oldest first — every put and
every delete marker up to the bucket's History depth. 404 when the bucket
does not exist or the key was never written.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

name: get_v1_pubsub_kv_bucket_key_history

description:
CreateStream creates a durable stream capturing the given subjects and
returns it. 409 when the org already has a stream of that name; the subjects
are the org's own and cannot collide with another org's.

name.description: Name is the stream's name within the org: 1–64 of [A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

name: post_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams

description:
CreateConsumer creates a durable consumer on one stream and returns it. A
consumer is a named cursor: it tracks what has been delivered and what is
acknowledged, so many workers can share it and none sees a message twice
outside redelivery. 409 when the stream already has a consumer of that name
with a different configuration.

name.description: Name is the durable consumer name: 1–64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-].

stream.description: Stream is the stream to consume, from the path.

name: post_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream_consumers

description:
Fetch pulls the next batch from a consumer and acknowledges it — the
request/response way to consume a stream. The hand-off is at-most-once: a
message returned here is acked here, so a caller that loses the response does
not see it again. Workers needing at-least-once delivery consume the same
consumer over the NATS port, where acks are theirs to send. An empty batch
after the wait is an empty page, not an error.

batch.description:
Batch is the most messages to return. 0 or less means 1; anything above
100 is clamped to 100.

name.description: Name is the consumer, from the path.

stream.description: Stream is the stream, from the path.

waitMs.description:
WaitMs is how long to wait for the batch to fill before answering with
what arrived. 0 or less means the default of 5000; clamped to 30000.

name: post_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream_consumers_name_next

description:
CreateBucket creates a KV bucket and returns it. A bucket is keyed state on
the same durable plane as the streams: each key holds up to History
revisions, entries can expire by TTL, and watchers on the NATS port see every
write. 409 when the org already has a bucket of that name.

bucket.description:
Bucket is the bucket's name within the org, from the path: 1–64 of
[A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

history.description: History is how many revisions each key keeps, 1–64. 0 means 1.

maxValue.description:
MaxValue caps one value's size in bytes. 0 or less means the server's
ceiling.

ttl.description: TTL expires entries after this many SECONDS. 0 means no expiry.

name: post_v1_pubsub_kv_bucket

description:
Publish puts one message on the org's bus. When a stream captures the subject
the write is DURABLE — the receipt names the stream and sequence only after
JetStream has it on storage, and a repeated Nats-Msg-Id header within the
dedup window answers duplicate instead of storing twice. When nothing
captures it, the message goes out core NATS: delivered to current
subscribers, receipt {ok}, nothing retained.

data.description:
Data is the payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).
Binary payloads belong on the NATS port.

headers.description:
Headers are optional message headers, one value per name. A Nats-Msg-Id
header is JetStream's deduplication key: a repeat within the stream's
dedup window is acknowledged as duplicate rather than stored twice.

subject.description:
Subject is the subject to publish to, in the org's own namespace — e.g.
orders.created. No wildcards.

name: post_v1_pubsub_publish

description:
Request sends one request on the org's bus and waits for one reply — the
synchronous half of pub/sub, for callers speaking to a responder subscribed
on the NATS port. 404 when nobody is listening on the subject; 408 when a
responder exists but no reply arrived within the timeout.

data.description: Data is the request payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text.

headers.description: Headers are optional request headers, one value per name.

subject.description: Subject is the subject a responder listens on, in the org's namespace.

timeoutMs.description:
TimeoutMs bounds the wait for a reply. 0 or less means the default of
5000; anything above 30000 is clamped to 30000.

name: post_v1_pubsub_request

description:
UpdateStream rewrites a stream's configuration — subjects, limits, discard —
and returns the updated stream. It is a PUT: the spec sent replaces the spec
held, with one reading for the enums a caller omits — an empty storage,
retention or discard keeps the stream's current one, because JetStream holds
storage and retention immutable and refuses a change with a 400 rather than
this door pretending it took.

stream.description: Stream is the stream to update, from the path.

name: put_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream

description:
Put sets one key to one value and returns the revision the write created.
Writes are versioned: each put is a new revision and the bucket retains up to
its History of them per key.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

value.description: Value is the value, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).

name: put_v1_pubsub_kv_bucket_key
